The court declared Utomi’s plan to be unconstitutional and unknown to Nigeria’s presidential system.
A Federal High Court sitting in Abuja on Monday declared Professor Pat Utomi’s plan to form a “shadow government” in Nigeria as unconstitutional.
The court declared Utomi’s plan to be unconstitutional and unknown to Nigeria’s presidential system.
In a ruling delivered on Monday, Justice James Omotosho declared that the notion of a “shadow government” or alternative cabinet “is alien to the Nigerian Constitution and has no legal basis.”
The judgment followed a suit filed by the State Security Service (SSS), also known as the Department of State Services (DSS).
The court consequently barred Professor Pat Utomi, a political economist and former presidential aspirant, along with his associates, from pursuing the initiative. Justice Omotosho emphasized that the proposal conflicts with Nigeria’s presidential system and has the potential to mislead the public, noting that the Constitution does not provide for any parallel or alternative government outside the one it establishes.
“Section 14(2)(c) makes no allowance for a shadow government. The defendant cannot import foreign constitutional models to confuse Nigerians. Such a so-called shadow government is hereby declared null and void,” Justice Omotosho held.
The dispute between the DSS and Professor Utomi, a former 2007 presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), arose after the agency filed a lawsuit challenging his plan to form a shadow government, describing it as unconstitutional.
The DSS, Nigeria’s domestic intelligence agency, sought to prevent Utomi and his associates from pursuing the initiative.
Utomi opposed the suit, arguing that his plan fell within his constitutional rights to freedom of expression and association, and that stopping it would infringe on those rights.
Recognising the novel nature of the case, Justice James Omotosho invited seven senior lawyers to serve as amici curiae (friends of the court) to guide the delivery of judgment.
During the July 10 hearing, the submissions from the legal experts were sharply divided. Some supported the DSS’s stance, while others defended Utomi’s proposal as a legitimate civic initiative. After considering their arguments, the judge reserved judgment until today (September 29).
In his ruling, Justice Omotosho acknowledged that the defendant is entitled to his fundamental rights but emphasised that these rights are not absolute and must operate within constitutional limits.
He concluded that the formation of a shadow government exceeds those limits and is capable of causing societal disruption.

Dans le cadre du projet « Jouer Pour Apprendre/Play to Learn », financé par l’USAID et mis en œuvre par Mott MacDonald,le ministère de la femme et de la famille a réuni le 29 et 30 septembre dernier au Sheraton hôtel, les acteurs liés à la mise en œuvre de la politique nationale de l’enfance pour évaluer les progrès réalisés et identifier notamment les priorités pour 2025.
Le Sheraton hôtel a abrité un atelier crucial pour l’avenir des enfants. Organisé par le ministère de la femme et de la famille dans le cadre du projet « Jouer Pour Apprendre/Play to Learn », financé par l’USAID et mis en œuvre par l’organisation Mott MacDonald, a réuni sur place l’ensemble des acteurs en charge de la mise en œuvre de la politique nationale de l’enfance dont les principaux sont issus de l’éducation, de la santé et de la justice. L’événement, qui s’est tenu le 29 et 30 septembre passé, visait justement à renforcer le suivi des indicateurs de la Politique Nationale de l’Enfance (PNE) et à préparer la prochaine phase de mise en œuvre, avec en ligne de mire l’objectif ambitieux de garantir à chaque enfant de grandir dans un environnement propice à son développement.
Cet atelier multisectoriel qui s’inscrit dans la continuité des efforts amorcés en 2023 permettrait d’évaluer les progrès réalisés dans la mise en œuvre des indicateurs de la PNE pour la période 2023-2025, d’identifier notamment les défis pour l’année 2025 et d’élaborer des solutions concrètes pour les surmonter.
Au cours de la cérémonie inaugurale de cet atelier, le chef de Projet « Jouer pour Apprendre », de l’USAID, Dr. Romain Babagbeto, a souligné l’importance cruciale de cet événement dans le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles pour un suivi efficace des indicateurs de la PNE. Il a également rappelé l’engagement fort de l’USAID et de Mott MacDonald aux côtés du gouvernement djiboutien pour garantir un accès élargi et équitable à une éducation de qualité pour la petite enfance, un objectif primordial pour Djibouti à l’horizon 2030. S’exprimant au nom du ministère de la femme et de la famille, Ousman Djama Osman alors conseiller juridique de ce département, a lui aussi mis l’accent sur l’importance de cet atelier pour garantir l’efficacité de la PNE. « La Politique Nationale de l’Enfance est l’une des pierres angulaires de notre développement. Pour que chaque enfant puisse grandir dans un environnement sécurisé et propice à son épanouissement, nous devons disposer d’indicateurs fiables pour suivre nos progrès et ajuster nos actions en fonction des besoins», a-t-il plaidé. Le juriste a également mis en avant l’importance d’une collaboration intersectorielle solide. « Que vous veniez de l’éducation, de la santé ou de la justice, chaque secteur a un rôle crucial à jouer. La coopération entre ces différents domaines est la clé pour assurer un suivi rigoureux de la PNE et pour garantir que nos efforts convergent vers le même objectif : le bien-être de chaque enfant djiboutien », a-t-il précisé. « Nous avons le devoir, en tant que décideurs, parents, éducateurs et partenaires, de garantir à chaque enfant un bon départ dans la vie. L’avenir de notre nation en dépend », a-t-il déclaré pour conclure.
Les discussions et les présentations animées par les représentants du Ministère de la Femme et de la Famille, dont M. Ismaël Mohamed, Conseiller Technique, M. Osman Djama, Conseiller Juridique, et Mme Zam-Zam Hassan Farah, Directrice de la Planification et du Suivi-Évaluation au cours de ces deux jours ont permis de faire le point sur les indicateurs de la PNE et de proposer des actions concrètes pour leur amélioration.
Les participants ont validé les indicateurs collectés et proposé des ajustements pour optimiser le suivi. Parmi les résultats notables, les acteurs ont élaboré un plan d’action clair pour le prochain trimestre, incluant la répartition des responsabilités entre les parties prenantes. Cela permettra de s’assurer que les données collectées soient à jour et pertinentes, facilitant ainsi la prise de décisions éclairées pour l’avenir de la PNE. Par ailleurs, des solutions ont été proposées pour le renforcement des capacités des acteurs du domaine.
La collaboration intersectorielle, clé du succès de la mise en œuvre de la PNE, a été mise en avant lors des débats. Les participants, provenant des secteurs de l’éducation, de la santé et de la justice, ont partagé leurs expériences et propositions pour améliorer la coordination entre les différents secteurs.
RACHID BAYLEH

The Sheraton hotel hosted a workshop crucial for the future of children. Organised by the Ministry of Women and Family as part of the "Jouer Pour Apprendre/Play to Learn" project, funded by USAID and implemented by the organisation Mott MacDonald, it brought together on site all the actors in charge of implementing the national child policy, the main ones coming from education, health and justice. The event, which was held on 29 and 30 September, was aimed precisely at strengthening the monitoring of the indicators of the National Child Policy (PNE) and at preparing the next phase of implementation, with the ambitious goal in sight of guaranteeing that every child grows up in an environment conducive to their development.

This multisectoral workshop, which follows on from the efforts begun in 2023, would make it possible to assess the progress made in implementing the PNE indicators for the period 2023-2025, to identify in particular the challenges for 2025 and to develop concrete solutions to overcome them.

During the inaugural ceremony of this workshop, the head of the USAID "Jouer pour Apprendre" project, Dr. Romain Babagbeto, underlined the crucial importance of this event in strengthening institutional capacities for effective monitoring of the PNE indicators. He also recalled the strong commitment of USAID and Mott MacDonald alongside the Djiboutian government to guarantee broad and equitable access to quality early childhood education, a primary objective for Djibouti by 2030. Speaking on behalf of the Ministry of Women and Family, Ousman Djama Osman, then legal adviser of that department, also stressed the importance of this workshop in ensuring the effectiveness of the PNE. "The National Child Policy is one of the cornerstones of our development. For every child to be able to grow up in a secure environment conducive to their flourishing, we must have reliable indicators to track our progress and adjust our actions according to needs," he pleaded. The lawyer also highlighted the importance of solid intersectoral collaboration. "Whether you come from education, health or justice, each sector has a crucial role to play. Cooperation between these different fields is the key to ensuring rigorous monitoring of the PNE and to guaranteeing that our efforts converge towards the same objective: the well-being of every Djiboutian child," he specified. "We have the duty, as decision-makers, parents, educators and partners, to guarantee every child a good start in life. The future of our nation depends on it," he declared in conclusion.

The discussions and presentations led by the representatives of the Ministry of Women and Family, including Mr Ismael Mohamed, Technical Adviser, Mr Osman Djama, Legal Adviser, and Mrs Zam-Zam Hassan Farah, Director of Planning and Monitoring-Evaluation, over these two days made it possible to take stock of the PNE indicators and to propose concrete actions for their improvement.

The participants validated the indicators collected and proposed adjustments to optimise monitoring. Among the notable results, the actors drew up a clear action plan for the next quarter, including the distribution of responsibilities among the stakeholders. This will make it possible to ensure that the data collected are up to date and relevant, thus facilitating informed decision-making for the future of the PNE. In addition, solutions were proposed for strengthening the capacities of the actors in the field.

Intersectoral collaboration, key to the success of the implementation of the PNE, was highlighted during the debates. The participants, coming from the education, health and justice sectors, shared their experiences and proposals for improving coordination between the different sectors.

አዲሱ ፈቃዱ (ዶ/ር) በአርባ ምንጭ ዩኒቨርሲቲ ተባባሪ ፕሮፈሰርና የእንሰት ፕሮጀክት አስተባባሪ እንደሚሉት፣ ብዙም ያልተወራለት ነገር ግን ከ25 ሚሊዮን በላይ ሕዝብ በቋሚ ምግብነት የሚጠቀሙት ተክል መሆኑን ተናግረዋል፡፡
የአርባ ምንጭ ዩኒቨርሲቲ እንሰትን የተመለከቱ በርካታ ችግሮችን ከአሥር ዓመታት አስቀድሞ ይቀርቡለት እንደነበርና ይህንንም መሠረት አድርጎ የዳሰሳ ጥናት ማድረጉን አስተባባሪው ይገልጻሉ፡፡
በዳሰሳ ጥናቱ ከተለዩ ችግሮች አንዱ እንሰቱን የመፋቂያው ሒደት የእናቶችን ጉልበትና ጊዜ የሚፈጅ እንደሆነ ነው፡፡ ሌላኛው ሲቀብሩ ጉድጓድ ስለሆነ የዚህ ናሙና ተወስዶ ሲታይ ለሰው ልጅ ለምግብነት ተስማሚ ያልሆኑ ነገሮች የሚገኙበት አጋጣሚ መኖሩ ነው፡፡
እንሰት ያለው ሰው ቆጮ የሚባለውን ምግብ ለማግኘት ሁለት ወርና ከዚያ በላይ ጊዜ መጠበቅ ግድ የሚሆንበት ሲሆን፣ ይህም ብቻ ሳይሆን ከተክሉ ውስጥ ለገበያ የሚቀርቡት ውጤቶች እሴት ያልተጨመረባቸውና ውስን መሆናቸው ነው፡፡ ይህንን መሠረት በማድረግ ጥናት የጀመረው የአርባ ምንጭ ዩኒቨርሲቲ በጥናቱም አዳዲስ የመፋቂያ ማሽኖች እንዲሠራ ማድረጉንና ይህም በአርሶ አደሩ ተሞክሮ በኢትዮጵያ የመጀመርያውን የወፍጮ የሙከራ ጣቢያ በአርባ ምንጭ ከተማ ዶርዜ ላይ እንደተቋቋመ አዲሱ (ዶ/ር) ተናግረዋል፡፡ በተጨማሪም በቤተ ሙከራ እርሾ በማበልፀግ ተክሉ ለምግብነት የሚፈጅበትን ጊዜ ወደ አንድ ሳምንት ዝቅ ማድረግ መቻሉን አስተባባሪው አክለዋል፡፡
ሌላውና ትልቁ ጉዳይ ከእንሰት እሴት የተጨመረባቸውን ምርቶች ማምረት ሲሆን በዚህም የእንሰት ዱቄት በመፈብረክ ከቡላና ከቆጮ ውጪ ከእንሰት ኬክ፣ ኩኪስ፣ ዳቦና የተፈለገውን ነገር ማምረት እንደሚቻል በተጨባጭ ተረጋግጧል፡፡ ይህም በርካታ የሥራ ዕድልና ገበያ ፈጥሯል፡፡
ፓተንት ያለውን የእንሰት ቴክኖሎጂ ፈጠራ የአሜሪካ የልማት ተራድኦ ድርጅት (USAID) በተለያዩ የአገሪቱ ክፍሎች እንዲስፋፋ አስፈላጊውን የቴክኒክና የፋይናንስ ድጋፍ ማድረጉ ታውቋል፡፡ ይህም ብቻ ሳይሆን የእንሰት ተረፈ ምርት በሆነው ቃጫ እናቶች ቱሪስትን መሠረት ያደረገ የተለያዩ ውጤቶችን እያመረቱ ለገበያ እንዲቀርቡ ማድረግ እንደተቻለ አዲሱ (ዶ/ር) አስረድተዋል፡፡
እስከተያዘው ዓመት ድረስ 32 የሚደርሱ የእንሰት ምርት ወፍጮ ቤቶች በመላ አገሪቱ የተቋቋሙ ሲሆን እነዚህም እንሰት አብቃይ በሚባሉት የሲዳማ፣ ደቡብ ኢትዮጵያ፣ ደቡብ ምዕራብ ኢትዮጵያ፣ ኦሮሚያና የማዕከላዊ ኢትዮጵያ ክልሎች ውስጥ ነው፡፡
አዲሱ (ዶ/ር) እንደሚሉት፣ በአገሪቱ ስንዴ ለማምረት በሚሊዮን የሚቆጠር ዶላር ለማዳበሪያ፣ ለአረም ማጥፊያ ኬሚካል ለመሳሰሉት ወጪ የሚደረግ ሲሆን፣ ነገር ግን እንሰት አንድም ዶላር የማይጠይቅ፣ ከውጭ የሚገባ ምንም ግብዓት የማይጠይቅ ተክል ነው፡፡
እንሰት በንጥረ ምግብ የበለፀገ፣ ኦርጋኒክ የሆነ፣ ግሉቲን ነጻ መሆኑ በዓለም አቀፍ ድርጅቶች የጥራት ማረጋገጫ የተሠራለት ስለመሆኑ የእንሰት ፕሮጀክት አስተባባሪው ለሪፖርተር አስረድተዋል፡፡
እንሰት ምንም ዶላር ሳይወጣበት በአንጻሩ በሚሊዮን የሚቆጠር ሀብት ወደ ውጪ መላክ የሚቻልበት ነው የሚሉት የእንሰት ፕሮጀክት አስተባባሪው፣ በዚህ ወቅት ዓለም አቀፍ የምግብ አምራቾች ፍላጎት ከማሳየት አልፈው ምርቱን ወስደውና ፈትሸው ለዓለም አቀፍ ገበያ ለማቅረብ ጥያቄ እያቀረቡ እንደሚገኙ ተናግረዋል፡፡
ቴክኒክና ሙያ ተቋማትን ጨምሮ የኢኖቬሽን ሚኒስቴር የባዮና ኢመርጂንግ ቴክኖሎጂ ኢንስቲትዩትና ሌሎችም ተቋማት ቴክኖሎጂውን ለማስፋት የሚደረገውን ጥረት እያገዙ መሆኑ ተጠቅሷል፡፡
‹የማሽኑ ፓተንት የእኛ ስለሆነ እንዴት እንደሚመረት እናሠለጥናለን፡፡ በዚህ መንገድ ለ20ዎቹ አካባቢዎች ወፍጮውን ያዳረስነው፡፡ አሁን ደግሞ በቅርቡ ለ40 አካባቢዎች እናደርሳለን የአጭር ጊዜ ዕቅዳችን 100 ለማድረስ ነው፤›› ሲሉ አዲሱ (ዶ/ር) አስታውቀዋል፡፡
ኢትዮጵያ ውስጥ ምርምር ከተሠራ በኋላ በታዋቂ ጆርናል ላይ ማሳተም እንደ መጨረሻ ግብ ተደርጎ ይወሳል የሚሉት አስተባባሪው፣ ትልቁ ግብ ሊሆን የሚገባው ምርምሩን ተጠቃሚው ጋር ማድረስ ነው፡፡ ያ ካልሆነ ተመራማሪዎች ለምርምር የሚያወጡት በጀት ሊመለስ እንደሚገባ አዲሱ (ዶ/ር) በጽኑ ያምናሉ፡፡
በቅርቡም አዲስ አበባ ላይ እሴት የተጨመረባቸው ከቆጮ የተገኙ ምርቶች መሸጫ ሱቅ እንደሚከፈት ታውቋል፡፡
በአርባ ምንጭ ዩኒቨርሲቲ የምርምር ዋና ዳይሬክተር የሆኑት ተስፋዬ ኃብተማርያም (ዶ/ር) በበኩላቸው በባህላዊ መንገድ የሚሠራው የእንሰት ምርት አድካሚ ከመሆኑ ባሻገር እስከ 45 በመቶ የሚሆነው ምርት ይባክናል ብለዋል፡፡ ነገር ግን የአርባ ምንጭ ዩኒቨርሲቲ አሻሽሎ የሠራው ማሽን እስከ 98 በመቶ ድረስ ብክነት የሌለው ምርት የሚገኝበት ነው፡፡ በሌላ በኩል ምርቱን የማብላላት ሒደት ከሁለት እስከ ስድስት ወር የሚፈጅ ሲሆን (እንሰት አብላለቶ ምግብ ለማድረግ) ይህን ችግር ለመፍታት የሚያስችልና በሳምንት ውስጥ አብላልቶ እንሰት ምግብ ለማድረግ የሚያስችል እርሾ መዘጋጀቱን ዋና ዳይሬክተሩ አስረድተዋል፡፡
እንሰት በደንብ ከተሠራበት የአገሪቱን የምግብ ችግር የሚፈታ እንደሆነ በልበ ሙሉነት የሚናገሩት ተስፋዬ (ዶ/ር)፣ በተጨማሪም የንጥረ ምግብ (Nutrition) ችግር ጭምር የሚፈታ ሲሆን በሚበቅልባቸውም ቦታዎች ልክ እንደ ዛፍ አካባቢን ለመጠበቅ ጭምር አማራጭ ሆኖ እንደሚቀርብ ያስረዳሉ፡፡
‹‹ለእንሰት የምናወጣው የኬሚካል ማዳበሪያ የለም፡፡ አገሪቱ ለኬሚካል ማዳበሪያ የምታወጣውን የውጭ ምንዛሪ መጠን እናውቀዋለን፡፡ ለእንሰት ግን ምንም ነገር የሚደረግለት ነገር የለም፡፡ ግፋ ቢል የተፈጥሮ ማዳበሪያ ፍግ ጥቅም ላይ ቢውል ነው፤›› ሲሉ ያስረዱት ተስፋዬ (ዶ/ር) ይህ በአገሪቱ የኢኮኖሚ ሁኔታ ላይ ትልቅ አስተዋጽኦ የሚያደርግ ነው ባይ ናቸው፡፡
አርባ ምንጭ ዩኒቨርሲቲ ያበለፀጋቸው የእንሰት ቴክኖሎጂዎች በሙሉ የተመለከተ አምስት የፈጠራ መብት ፓተንቶች እንዳገኘ የታወቀ ሲሆን በቀጣይ ማሽኑ በፋብሪካ ደረጃ እንዲመረትና እንዲበዛ በቀጣይ ጥረት ይደረጋል ተብሏል፡፡
ኢትዮጵያ ውስጥ የምግብ አጠቃቀም ችግር እንደሚስተዋል፣ በየዓመቱ የኅብረተሰብ ጤና ሳይንስ ኢንስቲትዩት የሚያወጣቸው ሪፖርቶች አስደንጋጭ እንደሆኑ፣ ዕድሜያቸው አምስትና አምስት ዓመት ያልሞላቸው ሕፃናት መቀንጨር በሚባለው ተጠቂ መሆናቸው አሳዛኝ ነው የሚሉት አዲሱ (ዶ/ር)፣ ምክንያቱም አገሪቱ ይህ ሁሉ ሀብት እያላት የሚከሰት መሆኑን በማስረዳት ነው፡፡
‹‹ኢትዮጵያ ውስጥ የምንበላቸው ምግቦች ስብጥራቸው ትንሽና በጣት የሚቆጠር ነው፡፡ እንሰት እኛ አገር እንደ እጥረት ናቸው ተብለው የሚጠቀሱት ማዕድናት በብዛት ይገኙበታል፡፡ ስለዚህ እንሰትን በዘመናዊ መልክ አቀናብረን ወደ ምግብ ሥርዓቱ ብንጨምር የተሻሻለ ይሆናል፤›› ሲሉ አዲሱ (ዶ/ር) ገልጸዋል፡፡
ብዙ ዕውቅና ያልተሰጣቸው እንደ ያም፣ ከሳቫ ሌሎችም በተለያዩ የአገሪቱ ክፍሎች የሚገኙ ተክሎችን ወደ ምግብ ሥርዓቱ ቢመጣ የሚገኘው ጥቅም ተዝቆ የማያልቅ እንደሆነ የሚናገሩት ባለሙያዎች፣ ያ ካልሆነ ማዳበሪያን ሁሌም ወደ አገር ውስጥ በማስገባት የምግብ ሉዓላዊነትን ማረጋገጥ አደጋች ነው ብለዋል፡፡
ከሳምንት አስቀድሞ ለተለያዩ የማኅበራዊ ትስስር ገጾችና በሌሎችም ሚዲያዎች ኢትዮጵያ የምግብ ሉዓላዊነቷን ችላለች የሚል መረጃ ሲናፈስ ተሰምቷል፡፡ ይህን በተመለከተ አስተያየታቸውን የሰጡት አዲሱ (ዶ/ር)፣ እሳቸውም ስለጉዳዩ በዜና ላይ መስማታቸውን ገልጸው፣ በተለያዩ ክልሎች ስለተመረተው የምርት መጠን ትክክለኛ መረጃ በሌለበት አስተያየት መስጠት እንደማይችሉ አስረድተዋል፡፡ ነገር ግን ጥራጥሬና የሰብል እህሎችን በብዛት ስለተመረተ ብቻ ራሳችንን በምግብ ችለናል ብሎ ለማውራት የሚያስደፍር እንዳልሆነ ግን ጠቅሰዋል፡፡
a4907.en:
It was disclosed that more than 25 million people use enset as a staple food

It was disclosed that the enset plant — rich in nutrients, gluten-free, and certified to quality standards by international quality-assurance organisations — is used as a staple food by more than 25 million people in Ethiopia.

According to Addisu Fekadu (PhD), associate professor at Arba Minch University and coordinator of the Enset Project, it is a plant that has been little talked about, yet is used as a staple food by more than 25 million people.

The coordinator explains that numerous problems relating to enset had been brought to Arba Minch University more than ten years ago, and that on that basis the university conducted a survey study.

One of the problems identified in the survey is that the process of scraping (decorticating) the enset consumes mothers' labour and time. Another is that, because it is buried in a pit, samples taken and examined have sometimes been found to contain matter unfit for human consumption.

A person with enset has to wait two months or more to obtain the food known as kocho; beyond that, the products from the plant that reach the market are limited and have no value added. On this basis Arba Minch University began its study, and Addisu (PhD) said that through the study new decorticating machines were developed, which were tried out by farmers, and that Ethiopia's first pilot milling station was established at Dorze in Arba Minch town. In addition, the coordinator added that by developing a starter culture in the laboratory it has been possible to reduce the time the plant takes to become edible to one week.

The other, bigger matter is producing value-added products from enset; it has been concretely confirmed that by producing enset flour it is possible to make, besides bula and kocho, cake, cookies, bread and whatever else one wants. This has created many jobs and markets.

It has become known that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) provided the necessary technical and financial support for the patented enset technology innovation to be expanded to various parts of the country. Moreover, Addisu (PhD) explained that it has been possible to enable mothers to produce various tourism-oriented products from the enset by-product fibre and bring them to market.

As of the current year, some 32 enset-product milling houses have been established across the country, in the enset-growing regions of Sidama, South Ethiopia, South West Ethiopia, Oromia and Central Ethiopia.

According to Addisu (PhD), millions of dollars are spent in the country on fertiliser, herbicides and the like in order to produce wheat, whereas enset is a plant that requires not a single dollar and requires no imported input.

The enset project coordinator explained to Reporter that enset is nutrient-rich, organic and gluten-free, and that this has been quality-certified by international organisations.

Saying that enset is something from which millions in wealth can be exported without any dollars being spent on it, the enset project coordinator said that at present international food producers have gone beyond showing interest — they have taken and tested the product and are requesting to bring it to the international market.

It was mentioned that the Ministry of Innovation's Bio and Emerging Technology Institute, along with technical and vocational institutions and other bodies, are assisting the effort to scale up the technology.

“Because the patent of the machine is ours, we train people in how it is produced. In this way we have distributed the mill to about 20 localities. Now we will soon deliver to 40 localities; our short-term plan is to reach 100,” Addisu (PhD) announced.

The coordinator, who says that in Ethiopia publishing in a well-known journal after research has been done is treated as the final goal, holds that the big goal should be delivering the research to the user. Addisu (PhD) firmly believes that if that does not happen, the budget researchers spend on research should be returned.

It has also become known that a shop selling value-added products derived from kocho will soon open in Addis Ababa.

For his part, Tesfaye Habtemariam (PhD), Director General of Research at Arba Minch University, said that besides being exhausting, the traditional method of producing enset wastes up to 45 percent of the product. But the machine improved and built by Arba Minch University yields a product with up to 98 percent waste-free processing. On the other hand, the fermentation process takes from two to six months (to ferment enset and turn it into food), and the Director General explained that a starter culture has been prepared that solves this problem and makes it possible to ferment enset into food within a week.

Tesfaye (PhD), who says confidently that if enset is properly worked on it will solve the country's food problem, explains that it also solves the nutrition problem and that, in the places where it grows, it serves like a tree as an option for protecting the environment.

“We spend nothing on chemical fertiliser for enset. We know the amount of foreign currency the country spends on chemical fertiliser. But for enset nothing whatsoever is applied. At most, natural manure might be used,” explained Tesfaye (PhD), who holds that this makes a great contribution to the country's economic situation.

It has become known that Arba Minch University has obtained five invention patents covering all the enset technologies it has developed, and it was said that efforts will be made going forward for the machine to be produced at factory scale and multiplied.

Addisu (PhD), who says that a problem of food utilisation is observed in Ethiopia, that the reports issued every year by the Public Health Institute are alarming, and that it is saddening that children under five years of age are victims of what is called stunting, explains that this is happening while the country has all this wealth.

“The foods we eat in Ethiopia are few in variety and can be counted on the fingers. Enset contains in abundance the minerals that are said to be deficient in our country. So if we process enset in a modern way and add it to the food system, it will be improved,” Addisu (PhD) said.

Experts who say that if plants found in various parts of the country that have been given little recognition — such as yam and cassava — were brought into the food system, the benefits obtained would be inexhaustible, said that otherwise it is dangerous to try to ensure food sovereignty by always importing fertiliser into the country.

A week ago, information circulated on various social media pages and in other media that Ethiopia had achieved its food sovereignty. Commenting on this, Addisu (PhD) said that he too had heard about the matter in the news, and explained that he could not comment in the absence of accurate information about the quantities produced in the various regions. He noted, however, that it is not something one can dare to claim — that we have achieved self-sufficiency in food merely because pulses and cereal crops were produced in quantity.

a4978.t:
Les rideaux sont tombés sur cette rencontre de haut niveau. C’était ce mercredi 29 novembre dans capitale burundaise. Elle avait pour objectif d’évaluer l’état d’exécution des recommandations de la 22ème réunion, tenue en mars dernier.
En outre, les responsables des banques d’émission au sein de la COMESA se sont penchés sur le fonctionnement de leur organisation. Leurs discussions ont porté également sur son budget, surtout sur les provisions budgétaires de sa chambre de compensation.
«Cette dernière se focalise sur la facilitation des échanges intra-Comesa pour réduire les coûts des transactions pour les opérateurs économiques des pays membres», a souligné Venuste Ndikumwenayo, directeur chargé des études et des statistiques à la Banque de la République du Burundi (BRB).
M. Ndikumwenayo indique que l’économie burundaise fait face à des rigidités structurelles. Ainsi, les importations sont très élevées par rapport aux exportations. Et de soutenir que le Burundi bénéficie de son appartenance à la COMESA. Il évoque l’intensification des échanges à des coûts de transactions réduits.
La présidence du Comité des gouverneurs de la COMESA pour l’année 2017 est assurée par le Burundi. L’année prochaine, il passera le flambeau au Djibouti.
a4978.en:
The curtain has come down on this high-level meeting. It took place this Wednesday, 29 November, in the Burundian capital. Its objective was to assess the state of implementation of the recommendations of the 22nd meeting, held last March.

In addition, the heads of the central banks within COMESA examined the functioning of their organisation. Their discussions also covered its budget, and in particular the budgetary provisions of its clearing house.

"The latter focuses on facilitating intra-COMESA trade in order to reduce transaction costs for economic operators in the member countries," stressed Venuste Ndikumwenayo, director in charge of research and statistics at the Bank of the Republic of Burundi (BRB).

Mr Ndikumwenayo notes that the Burundian economy faces structural rigidities. Imports are thus very high compared with exports. He maintains that Burundi benefits from its membership of COMESA, pointing to the intensification of trade at reduced transaction costs.

The chairmanship of the COMESA Committee of Governors for the year 2017 is held by Burundi. Next year, it will hand the torch to Djibouti.

Life Matters | May 27,2023

							By  BERSABEH GEBRE ( FORTUNE STAFF WRITER )  							
							
Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) can establish a business entity or be part of existing ones unrelated to their objectives to generate income. CSOs were only allowed to participate in areas that exclusively aligned with their objectives, to generate income and annual net profits that would back their finances.
A new bill hoped to regulate their income-generating mechanisms was issued three weeks ago following a discussion with the Authority for Civil Society Organizations (ACSO). CSO investments should not exceed 30pc of their annual budget, otherwise charged as an administrative cost. The administration costs should be less than 20pc of their annual budget while collecting money from schools, hospitals, and religious institutions is prohibited, and profits from business entities go to their charities.
Ten years ago, the Authority, formally known as the Ethiopian Charities & Civil Societies Agency, issued warnings to over 200 NGOs over budgetary breaches after conducting an investigation on 261 NGOs. It has found 192 of them spending more than 30pc of their budgets on administrative purposes and 12 local NGOs raising more than 10pc of their budgets from foreign sources, both passing limit.
The new directive extracted from the CSO law that was passed three years ago was authorized by the Ministry of Justice.
Under Jima Dilbo, the Authority oversees 4,400 CSOs, of which 570 are international organizations. Yonas Mesganaw, the legal advisor at the Authority, believes that the bill encourages CSOs to do business without the fear of breaching the agreement.
Formerly known as non-governmental organizations (NGOs), CSOs were sourcing budgets from donors and membership fees that were limited or unreliable.
According to the Director of the Consortium of Ethiopian Human Rights Organizations (CEHRO) Mesud Gebeyehu, fund disbursement is related to the relationship between donors and the nation, impacting the acceptance of proposals. He said expanding financial sources is the only way his organization will be secured. Established five years ago, the organization advocates for human rights, democracy, and peace, with 17 CSOs under its fleet.
Local organizations such as Kelem Ethiopia, engaged in the education sector, with limited-period projects mostly catering to specific groups, have mixed feelings. The General Director, Abdulaziz Arage, hopes that commercial banks will include CSOs in their loan portfolio though the bill is a step to alleviate their financial constraints.
The study conducted last year explained that in 2014, the total funds pledged by CSOs for 2,604 projects, excluding Dire Dewa city, accounted for 35.76 billion Br. The current fund for 2,885 projects under CSOs is committed to 78.87 billion Br. Only the Somali and Harari regional states experienced a decline in total budgets as some CSOs did not get the required license to operate.
Starting its operation in 2018, Pro Development Network (PDN) supports 50 CSOs. The network sources funds from international donors such as the European Union and USAID. The Director Ahmed Hussien, director general of PDN, said that their organization plans to rent machines that will be functional to dig holes for clean water projects.
"We are contacting donors to get those machines," he said.
He mentioned that some organizations struggle to get donations, making it difficult to implement their objectives.
Only Ethiopian-owned organizations can advocate for human rights issues, including the rights of children, women, and the disabled. They are required to obtain 90pc of their funds from local sources otherwise recognized as international organizations and prohibited from advocating on such issues.

There are growing concerns over the burden of malnutrition, including the severe forms in the northern part of the country.
Weekend Trust investigations revealed that many children and their parents are weighed down by the health implications of the burden of the condition as well as its socio-economic and long term effects.
The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) on Friday said lack of funding aggravated by President Donald Trump administration’s cuts to foreign aid would hinder the supply of lifesaving food to treat 80, 000 malnourished children in Nigeria within the next two months.
It said 1.3 million children under the age of five suffering from severe acute malnutrition risk losing access to lifesaving support this year in Ethiopia and Nigeria.
- Stop shortchanging Nigerians with palliatives
- Nigeria: Basically everything is corrupted — Onyema Ugochukwu
Experts blame inflation, food insecurity, others
Experts and nutrition focal organisations have harped on the need for urgent and holistic measures to address the menace.
They said the persistent malnutrition crisis in northern Nigeria stems from a variety of factors such as inflation, food insecurity, insufficient healthcare infrastructure, ongoing security issues and disease outbreaks compounded by low vaccine coverage.
UNICEF Nigeria Representative, Cristian Munduate, said nearly 5.4 million under-five children in the North West and North East are suffering from acute malnutrition, with projections indicating an additional one million cases by April 2025.
The UNICEF representative called on government to scale up nutrition interventions and promote child spacing initiatives to tackle the underlying challenge of rapid population growth.
Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said in 2024, its teams treated about 357,000 children suffering from malnutrition in the North.
“This is an increase of 35 per cent compared to the 265,500 children treated in 2023. Among those treated in 2024, 75,000 required inpatient care, while 282,000 received outpatient treatment. In 2024, the surge in malnutrition cases began as early as March, well before the usual peak season in July, and extended through November, a time when cases are typically expected to decline. This situation raises fears that the severity of malnutrition in 2025 could exceed that of previous years,” MSF said in a statement last month.
Its international president, Christos Christou, said the numbers in 2022 and 2023 were already critically high, adding that between January to August 2024, MSF saw a 51% increase in admissions of children with severe malnutrition, compared to the same period the previous year.
He said MSF also treated 52,725 children with severe malnutrition, a life-threatening condition across North in the first eight months of last year.
Speaking after his visit to MSF treatment centres in Maiduguri, Borno State, he said: “Unvaccinated children are particularly vulnerable to vaccine-preventable diseases, which elevate the risk of acute malnutrition.
Also, Save the Children International (SCI) said without an urgent action, an additional one million children in Nigeria would be suffering from acute malnutrition by next month.
Analysis of hunger data from Cadre Harmonisé showed that 5.4 million children are at risk of facing acute malnutrition by April, a 25% increase compared to the 4.4 per cent last year April
SCI said among them, about 1.8 million could be experiencing Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) – the deadliest form of malnutrition that compromises children’s immune systems and turns otherwise treatable illnesses, such as diarrhoea, potentially lethal. This represents an alarming 80% increase in SAM cases, it said.
The group also said the situation is particularly dire in the North West and the North East where ongoing conflict and insecurity are driving displacement and disrupting livelihoods.
Duncan Harvey, Save the Children’s Country Director for Nigeria, said, “In Nigeria, the crisis is reaching unprecedented levels as catastrophic climate disasters, escalating insecurity, and soaring prices threaten to leave over 16 million children hungry. Urgent action is essential to combat this devastating and unacceptable trend of child hunger and malnutrition and ensure a brighter future for Nigeria’s children.”
The organisation quoted Aisha, 27, mother of six, at the Save the Children’s clinic in Damaturu, as saying, “Hunger has entered my daughter’s body and she has emaciated terribly because I am unable to breastfeed her, I don’t produce breast milk. It has affected her growth compared to other children. We are grateful to Save the Children for the support at the centre.”
‘I’m worried hunger is hitting children’
Hajara, 15, a child campaigner from Katsina, said, “I am so worried about how food insecurity is hitting children in our community. With banditry everywhere, farmers cannot go to farms so food is getting harder to find. Lots of children go to bed hungry, and malnutrition level is high, leaving us tired and unable to concentrate in school. We need our leaders to step up, bring security back, and help us get the support we need so every child here can grow up safe, well-fed, and healthy.”
Aisha Abdullahi, a school teacher and mother of five in Kano, said she is worried.
“Malnutrition among school-age children is a major risk factor for low school enrolment, high absenteeism, early dropouts, and unsatisfactory classroom performance.
According to her, “I am a mother and I take care of children in school. Malnourished children are more prone to infections and illnesses, which can lead to missed school days and falling behind in their education,” she said.
Governments at all levels must rise to the occasion and address the problem. Children are the future of every society,” she said.
This year, 2025, it is predicted that 33 million people in Nigeria will not know where their next meal will come from including over 16 million children.
Daily Trust reports that hunger has risen sharply in Nigeria in recent years, up from about 7% of the population analysed by the UN in 2020 to 15% currently.
Also, it was gathered that the USAID 90-day funding freeze has affected some malnutrition interventions in the northern states, thereby leaving more children and their families at risk of malnutrition and hunger.
Families narrate ordeal
Murjanatu Bello from Gagi District took her daughter who was losing weight after having diarrhoea to Gagi Primary Health Centre, Sokoto State. The girl was tested and found out to be suffering from severe malnourishment.
“She initially started purging (diarrhoea). We took her to the nearest clinic where she was admitted for some days.
“Some days after we were discharged, we realised, she was losing weight and a woman from the neighbourhood advised that we should bring her to the clinic for a proper check-up.
“We then took her to Gagi clinic, where she was subjected to some tests and later confirmed to be suffering from severe malnourishment,” she narrated.
Another caregiver, Umaima Abu from Bubare village, said: “We spent a lot of money on traditional medicine without any improvement. We then decided to take him (her so) to the primary health centre, Gagi in Sokoto-South Local Government Area.
“He was given some drugs after which the health worker advised us to take him for Tamowa (malnutrition) test which we did. They put something on his hand and later told us our child was malnourished.
“They gave us the supplements free which we have been feeding him with. He is now recuperating.”
Similarly, Kulu Ardor from Lambo village in Kware Local Government Area, who brought her sick child for treatment, said: “He started losing weight; we spent some money treating him because we thought it was a different ailment, until we brought him to the hospital. We were given RUTF in the hospital which we were told was donated by one agency.
“We have been seeing some changes in him since he started taking it. He is getting well now.”
Holistic approach key to ending malnutrition in Borno, Yobe, Adamawa
UNICEF Chief of Borno Field Office, Dr. Tushar Rane, said children in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa states are battling escalating levels of malnutrition and there is need for immediate and holistic response to address it.
Quoting the 2023 lean season Nutrition and Food Security Surveillance (NFSS) Round 13 conducted across the three states, he said the prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM) among children under five years in Borno was 10.2%, 8.0% in Yobe and 4.0% in Adamawa.
This also means that an estimated 511, 807 children under five suffer from Severe Acute Malnutrition annually, requiring urgent interventions to save their lives, he said.
He said, “In our states, approximately 2.8 million children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) are in need of preventative nutrition services.”
‘Number of malnourished children in Kano alarming’
MSF said over 40,000 children were treated for malnutrition in Kano State in 2024.
Weekend Trust gathered that in response to the rising rates of malnutrition, MSF expanded its operations by opening outpatient treatment facilities in Kumbotso and Rijiyar Lemo, in addition to the one in Unguwa Uku.
According to the MSF project coordinator in Kano State, Hemmed Lukonge, “We are dealing with chronic and abnormal surge of severe acute malnutrition, children are coming from around 37 local government areas of Kano State and the state Ministry of Health does not have the necessary means in terms of nutrition supplies and human resources to address the matter.”
MSF advocated the establishment of outpatient feeding centres across all LGAs in Kano to enhance community-based management of malnutrition and reduce severe cases.
Malama Umaima Bello, a mother of one of the malnourished children at Unguwa Uku primary healthcare facility, said being at the facility had accorded her the chance to “understand the difference between food and nutritional food.”
She linked malnutrition, especially in the North, to food insecurity, poverty, poor knowledge of healthy feeding and high prevalence of vaccine preventable childhood illnesses like measles.
It was also gathered that there is an increase in internally displaced people / families in Kano, especially from neighbouring states that are experiencing security challenges among other issues. However, nutrition experts in the state said the main cause of food insecurity could be linked to decrease in agricultural activities due to climate change, high cost of living/ high inflation rate.
Director, Nutrition, Kano State Ministry of Health, Hajiya Rakiya Balarabe, said the state, in collaboration with various local and international agencies, is working to address malnutrition.
Bauchi to fight malnutrition with N100m
Recently, Executive Chairman of Bauchi State Primary Healthcare Development Board, Rilwanu Mohammed, said N100 million had been earmarked for nutrition activities
He said the Nigeria Demographic Health Survey 2023/2024 showed that the state had a high rate of malnourished children.
300, 000 children malnourished in Sokoto
About 300, 000 children are malnourished in Sokoto State, according to a UNICEF) report.
A service provider at Gagi PHC, Miqdat Ibrahim, attributed the surge in malnutrition cases to insecurity and poverty.
“Before the current economic and security issues, we were receiving between 70 and 135 cases, but the number increased significantly because of the presence of IDP camp in Gagi,” he said.
Zamfara
Also, the UNICEF Country Representative, Christen Muduate, recently said 250,000 out of 1.2 million children in Zamfara were battling malnutrition.
She said one out of every 10 children in the state was staring at death, while stunting among children aged between 0 and five years was at an alarming rate of 45.2 per cent.
“In Zamfara, we are intending to treat 400,000 under five children suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition. 200,000 additional children in the North-West will require Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) in 2025, compared to 2024,” she said.
Implications of malnutrition in children
UNICEF’s Nutrition Officer in Abuja, Nkeiruka Enwelum, said, “Inadequate nutrition has lots of consequences on general health and wellbeing. There is also the implication of increased mortality, especially in children less than three years of age and in women of reproductive age as the main population groups of concern.
“The foods that we eat give us different things in our bodies. Failure to eat some of these things in the right quantities can result in poor growth and development in the body.”
Nemat Hajeebhoy, Chief of Nutrition, UNICEF Nigeria, said investing in malnutrition translates to investing in brain development and the human capital of a country.
“Therefore, it is absolutely vital and critical to our growth. If you have children and you don’t feed them well, they will not be able to grow well,” the official said.
How to reduce burden of malnutrition
Save the Children called on governments to tackle food shortages, stabilise rising prices and increase protection for farmers facing violence from armed groups.
“Governments also need to address the climate crisis by building communities’ resilience, as well as more awareness and early warning for people to prepare for climate induced disasters,” the organisation said.
Experts at MSF urged strengthening healthcare facilities to diagnose and treat malnutrition, reinforcing vaccine programmes, enhancing access to nutritious food, improving water and sanitation, and raising awareness.

Por: Carlos Carvalho
O 25 de Abril de 1974, marcou o fim da guerra nas colónias portuguesas.
A Luta de Libertação dos Povos das colónias chegara ao fim, depois de mais de uma dezena de anos.
Um complicado período, que se convencionou designar “de transição”, se seguiu nos diferentes espaços.
A Luta e esse período acabaram por conduzi-las às independências, em 1975.
Assim, és tudu kuaji ta completa 50 anu.
São estes “cinquentões” a quem me refiro nesta reflexão.
HISTÓRIA DIFERENCIADA
Dirigidos pelo PAIGC, de Cabral; MPLA/FNLA/UNITA, Angola, de Neto, Holden e Savimbi; FRELIMO, Moçambique, de Mondlane e Machel; e MLSTP, de Pinto da Costa, dentre estes países-novo-nascidos, só a Guiné escreveu uma história diferente.
Uma luta de libertação exemplar fez com que a Guiné se autoproclamasse independente ainda em 1973, constituindo assim a única excepção no critério “acesso a independência”.
Em 1975, aquando da independência, de jure, dos outros territórios, a Guiné já era reconhecida pa kuazi tudu mundu.
Vamos por partes.
PERIODO DE TRANSIÇÃO
ANGOLA
Para chegar a independência, Angola teve nos 3 Movimentos, 3 pretendentes ao louro de Movimento-Líder e, consequentemente, seu líder assumir a liderança do país. Uma longa e violenta luta fratricida se abriu, luta que durou décadas até ao desaparecimento do Chefe da UNITA.
Angola conheceu, durante estes 50 anos, 3 Presidentes, sempre com o mesmo Partido no poder.
CABO VERDE
O processo independentista-berdianu foi seguramente o mais complicado. O PAIGC sempre teve problemas em gerir esse processo.
Para tentar acalmar os ânimos dos “impacientes independentistas-berdianus”, chegou até a formar dezenas de jovens para um “Desembarque”, à Fidel em Cuba, desembarque k caba pa ca contisi.
Pela sua localização estratégica, as ilhas caírem nas mãos dos comunistas seria de todo inaceitável.
O novo poder em Portugal não pretende, de forma alguma, abrir mão da sua “joia-das-colónias”.
É pressionado a não ceder, mas, o curso da história estava traçado.
PAIGC cá luta 11 anu pá Guiné k Kau Berdi pá, na fin, sair só com um dos motivos de sua luta.
Um intenso período de transição se viveu nas ilhas, acabando o PAIGC por se impor e assumir, a solo, a independência das ilhas.
MOÇAMBIQUE
Moçambique terá sido menos complexo que o caso de Cabo Verde. A FRELIMO chega a independência como única força lutadora para esse desiderato. O processo “independentário” não foi tão conturbado como, por exemplo, em Angola, onde as armas nunca calaram.
SÃO TOMÉ
São Tomé e Príncipe, seguramente, foi mais pacifico ainda, com o MLSTP assumindo o caminho para a independência.
GUINÉ
A Guiné é, de todo, um caso “aparte”.
A se considerar 1975, a Guiné é o “irmão-mais-velho” das 5 colonias, no que tange a idade de Nação Livre e Independente.
Chegados a independência, a história dos 5 mudou.
DENOMINADORES–COMUNS
Porém, há/houve casos que podemos considerar de “denominadores-comuns”.
Os “Partidos-históricos” assumiram a gestão dos países recém-independentes.
Todos esses Partidos se transformaram naquilo que entrou na história como Partido-Único.
Os Países-maiores dos 5 continuam, até hoje, sendo dirigidos pelos “Partidos-históricos”.
Em todos, nos anos 90, instalou-se a democracia.
Em 2, os “Partidos-históricos” nunca saíram do poder (Angola e Moçambique)
Em 3, houve alternâncias no poder (Cabo Verde, Guiné, e S. Tomé e Príncipe)
BONS E MAUS CINQUENTÕES
Depois das independências, Os-5 escreveram outras narrativas; as histórias raras vezes se convergiram, mesmo que, seguindo ainda o exemplo das lutas de libertação, criaram uma organização a que deram o nome de PALOP, para concertarem suas políticas.
Esta organização, pá nós, cá merece li…nen un atenson!!
Era meu desejo juntar os “Cinquentões”, para obviar esta reflexão, mas não seria fácil. Os percursos foram, como dito anteriormente, diferenciados.
De facto, há um único bom-cinquentão pelo que não vou dedicar-lhe muita atenção. Bastas são os elogios que o mundo lhe dedica.
E…caba de subi más un degrau, Médio-Alto, no seio das nações do mundo.
Ao contrário, há um “mau-cinquentão” a quem vou dedicar mais atenção. Todos já sabem a que “cinquentão” me refiro.
POS-INDEPENDÊNCIA
ANGOLA + MOÇAMBIQUE
Estes dois “cinquentões”, apesar de terem enfrentado décadas de duras lutas fratricidas, nunca conheceram os famosos “golpes-de-estado”.
Essa longa luta entre irmãos fez com que não tivessem atingido as aspirações de vida melhor que os seus cidadãos esperavam conhecer “pós-ida dos tugas”.
Todos os dados das organizações internacionais demonstram isso: no ensino, na saúde, na infraestruturação do país, etc., etc.
Tudo pode ser desculpado por essa guerra, adicionando a notória má-governação dos seus dirigentes, com alegadas corrupções graves minando todo o aparelho de estado.
S. TOMÉ E PRINCIPE
S. Tomé é um caso raro.
Sem aparentes motivos para tal, sempre andou em turbulências, com ameaças e mais ameaças de golpes; com golpes palacianos-constitucionais reais, o país viveu sempre na instabilidade.
Felizmente, nunca descambou em guerra entre irmãos. Raras as vezes os partidos ganhadores das eleições cumprem o mandato.
Mas, nisto, o Pior-Cinquentão-mesmo…é:
MINHA-OUTRA-TERRA
Ayan!!
A “minha-outra-terra” é campeão de mau-aluno, campeão de “mau-cinquentão”!!
Na verdade, cumesa midjor k tudu és.
Na boca-mundo, graças à sua brilhante LLN e ao seu líder, “nha-utru-terra” txiga anu 80 de século 20, k fama na mundu.
Mama Djombo, famoso conjunto guineense cantou:
Pikinu na tamanhu…ma garandi na fama
1980
Má sima pá azar, começou a doença dos golpes.
Foi no já longínquo ano 80.
Mata-riba-di-mata; golpi-riba-di-golpi; guerra-civil: tudu di mau kontisi na “minha-outra-terra”!
“Minha-outra-terra” nunca mais “apanhou pé” di sua cabeça!!
Enquanto todos os “Cinquentões-turbulentos”…ultimo foi nós mansus-amigus-moçambicanos…estão tirando cabeça da água, “nha-utru-terra” teima em se enterrar na lama.
Povo, de tanto “cá panha pé” di sua cabeça, em vez de escolher um brilhante-líder, resolveu escolher um Presidente “fajuto”, “tranbikeru”, despreparado, enfim!!
O Presidente resolveu…já tinha resolvido…ser Ditador!!
Ele é o Único; Omnipresente; Omnipotente!!
Txuba cai…é SE
Sol sai…é General
Bentu supra…é Presi
Mar intxi…é El-Moctar
Mar baxa…
Má “minha-outra-terra” caba na nada!!
Todo o mundo tem medo do General
General tem alcance até para mandar mi sotar…mi li na Txada xintadu.
Políticos, tudu k medu.
Manda prender-bazar gaz-sotar-“fuguiar”.
Nin mancara ca ta quebra, como se diz na minha-outra-terra!!!
E…é recebido em todos os palácios do mundo.
Ele é…tu-ca-tu-la com: rapasinhu-Macron; Ntoni-Goes; Patakeru-Rebelo-di-Souza; Mufinu-Neves; Macambuzio-Lourenço; teatrista-Zilensky, até com Sotador-Putin!!
Pantimineru, como é, até já foi fazer paz:
Na Leste; na Gaza; na Iron-Israel!!
Já prometeu pôr o Doido-Trump na linha se este “dar-para-doido”!!
Enfim!!!
E…já foi convidado para vir assistir ao nosso cinquentenário.
Ah, Cabral!!!
Pa ké k bu dá bu vida!!!!???
Bando di labregus dirigindo teu país!!
Mandato do Ditador acabou.
Resolveu ma ca sa ta sai di Polasiu…
Lá está!!
Forti tristeza!!
E…
CPLP-PALOP
Estas organizações que não existem vão para o Palácio-do-Ditador dar-lhe “curu” di Presidente da CPLP.
E…querem que o Povo-da-CPLP vos leve a sério.
Os Presidentes vão legitimar um Ditador, tornando-o Presidente da CPLP.
Paxenxa!!
CONCLUINDO
50 anu dja passa.
Un sta rei-di-bon; otus, más-o-menus; otus, na labi-labi…na lama!!
Meus desejos é que todos estejam, nos próximos pelo menos dez anos, como estão estas 10 ilhas fuliadas na meio-Atlântico.
Tivemos a sorte de, desde o início, sermos geridos por gente-que-ama-sua-terra. Gente que deixou tudo para fazer este povo feliz.
Eles são todos, hoje, setentões/oitentões/noventões!!
Boa parte não está no mundo dos vivos.
A vós, dedico este artigo…esta reflexão!!
E…Sarava…cinquentões!!

By: Carlos Carvalho
The 25th of April 1974 marked the end of the war in the Portuguese colonies.
The Liberation Struggle of the Peoples of the colonies had come to an end, after more than a dozen years.
A complicated period, which came to be called "transitional," followed in the various territories.
The Struggle and that period ultimately led them to independence in 1975.
So, all of them are almost completing 50 years.
It is these "fifty-somethings" that I refer to in this reflection.
A DIFFERENTIATED HISTORY
Led by the PAIGC, of Cabral; the MPLA/FNLA/UNITA in Angola, of Neto, Holden and Savimbi; FRELIMO in Mozambique, of Mondlane and Machel; and the MLSTP, of Pinto da Costa - among these newly born countries, only Guinea wrote a different history.
An exemplary liberation struggle led Guinea to proclaim itself independent as early as 1973, thus constituting the only exception in the criterion of "access to independence."
In 1975, when the other territories became independent de jure, Guinea was already recognised by almost the whole world.
Let us take it step by step.
TRANSITION PERIOD
ANGOLA
To reach independence, Angola had, in its 3 Movements, 3 contenders for the laurel of Leading Movement and, consequently, for its leader to assume the leadership of the country. A long and violent fratricidal struggle broke out, a struggle that lasted decades until the disappearance of the UNITA Chief.
Angola has known, during these 50 years, 3 Presidents, always with the same Party in power.
CABO VERDE
The Cape Verdean independence process was surely the most complicated. The PAIGC always had problems managing that process.
To try to calm the tempers of the "impatient Cape Verdean independence supporters," it even went so far as to train dozens of young people for a "Landing," Fidel-style as in Cuba, a landing that in the end never took place.
Because of its strategic location, the islands falling into the hands of the communists would have been altogether unacceptable.
The new power in Portugal had no intention whatsoever of giving up its "jewel of the colonies."
It was pressured not to give in, but the course of history had already been traced.
The PAIGC fought here for 11 years for Guinea and Cape Verde, only to end up, in the end, achieving only one of the aims of its struggle.
An intense transition period was lived through in the islands, with the PAIGC ending up imposing itself and taking on, alone, the independence of the islands.
MOZAMBIQUE
Mozambique will have been less complex than the case of Cape Verde. FRELIMO arrives at independence as the only fighting force for that aim. The "independence" process was not as troubled as, for example, in Angola, where the guns never fell silent.
SAO TOME
Sao Tome and Principe was surely even more peaceful, with the MLSTP taking on the path to independence.
GUINEA
Guinea is, altogether, a case "apart."
If 1975 is taken as the reference, Guinea is the "elder brother" of the 5 colonies, as regards its age as a Free and Independent Nation.
Once independence was reached, the history of the 5 changed.
COMMON DENOMINATORS
However, there are/were cases that we may consider "common denominators."
The "historic Parties" took over the management of the newly independent countries.
All those Parties turned into what went down in history as the Single Party.
The largest countries of the 5 continue, to this day, to be led by the "historic Parties."
In all of them, in the 1990s, democracy was installed.
In 2 of them, the "historic Parties" never left power (Angola and Mozambique).
In 3 of them, there were alternations in power (Cape Verde, Guinea, and Sao Tome and Principe).
GOOD AND BAD FIFTY-SOMETHINGS
After the independences, The-5 wrote other narratives; their histories rarely converged, even though, still following the example of the liberation struggles, they created an organisation to which they gave the name PALOP, in order to coordinate their policies.
This organisation, for us, deserves here... not a bit of attention!!
It was my wish to bring the "Fifty-somethings" together, to frame this reflection, but it would not be easy. Their paths were, as said earlier, differentiated.
In fact, there is only one good fifty-something, so I will not devote much attention to it. Plentiful are the praises the world devotes to it.
And... it has just climbed one more step, to Middle-High, among the nations of the world.
On the contrary, there is a "bad fifty-something" to whom I will devote more attention. Everyone already knows which "fifty-something" I am referring to.
POST-INDEPENDENCE
ANGOLA + MOZAMBIQUE
These two "fifty-somethings," despite having faced decades of harsh fratricidal struggles, never knew the famous "coups d'etat."
That long struggle between brothers meant that they did not attain the aspirations of a better life that their citizens expected to know "after the departure of the Portuguese."
All the data of the international organisations show this: in education, in health, in the country's infrastructure, etc., etc.
Everything can be excused by that war, adding to it the notorious bad governance of their leaders, with alleged serious corruption undermining the whole apparatus of the state.
SAO TOME AND PRINCIPE
Sao Tome is a rare case.
With no apparent reasons for it, it has always been in turbulence, with threats and more threats of coups; with real palace-constitutional coups, the country has always lived in instability.
Fortunately, it never degenerated into war between brothers. Rarely do the parties that win the elections complete their mandate.
But, in this, the truly Worst-Fifty-something... is:
MY-OTHER-LAND
Alas!!
"My-other-land" is the champion of the bad pupil, champion of the "bad fifty-something"!!
In truth, it began better than all of them.
In the mouth of the world, thanks to its brilliant LLN and to its leader, "my-other-land" reached the 1980s of the 20th century with fame in the world.
Mama Djombo, the famous Guinean band, sang:
Small in size... but great in fame
1980
But as if by bad luck, the disease of coups began.
It was in the now distant year of 1980.
Killing upon killing; coup upon coup; civil war: everything bad happened in "my-other-land"!
"My-other-land" never again got its head above water!!
While all the "turbulent Fifty-somethings" - the last were our gentle Mozambican friends - are getting their heads out of the water, "my-other-land" insists on burying itself in the mud.
The People, from so much failing to get on their feet, instead of choosing a brilliant leader, decided to choose a "fake," "swindler," unprepared President, in short!!
The President decided... he had already decided... to be a Dictator!!
He is the Only One; Omnipresent; Omnipotent!!
Rain falls... it is HE
The sun comes out... it is the General
The wind blows... it is the Presi
The tide comes in... it is El-Moctar
The tide goes out...
But "my-other-land" ends up with nothing!!
Everybody is afraid of the General
The General has reach enough even to have me arrested... me here sitting in Chada.
Politicians, all of them afraid.
He orders arrests, expulsions, tear gas, shooting.
Not even a peanut gets cracked, as they say in my-other-land!!!
And... he is received in every palace in the world.
He is on first-name terms with: little-boy-Macron; Antonio-Guterres; blowhard-Rebelo-de-Sousa; wretched-Neves; sullen-Lourenco; play-actor-Zelensky, even with Shooter-Putin!!
Shameless as he is, he has even gone off to make peace:
In the East; in Gaza; in Iron-Israel!!
He has already promised to bring Crazy-Trump into line if the latter "goes crazy"!!
Anyway!!!
And... he has already been invited to come and attend our fiftieth anniversary.
Ah, Cabral!!!
What did you give your life for!!!!??
A bunch of yokels running your country!!
The Dictator's mandate has ended.
He has decided that he is not leaving the Palace...
There you have it!!
Great sadness!!
And...
CPLP-PALOP
These organisations that do not exist go to the Dictator's Palace to give him the "crown" of President of the CPLP.
And... they want the People of the CPLP to take them seriously.
The Presidents are going to legitimise a Dictator, making him President of the CPLP.
Patience!!
IN CONCLUSION
50 years have already passed.
One is doing really well; others, more or less; others, crawling... in the mud!!
My wish is that all of them may be, over the next at least ten years, as these 10 islands scattered in the middle of the Atlantic are.
We had the good fortune of being governed, from the outset, by people who love their land. People who gave up everything to make this people happy.
They are all, today, seventy-, eighty-, ninety-somethings!!
A good part of them are no longer among the living.
To you I dedicate this article... this reflection!!
And... Sarava... fifty-somethings!!
30/06/2025

Moçambique importou arroz equivalente a 4,1 mil milhões de meticais apenas no primeiro trimestre deste ano, segundo dados do Banco de Moçambique (BdM). Este valor representa quase 15% do total de bens de consumo adquiridos no exterior, no mesmo período, mantendo o arroz como um dos três produtos mais importados no país. O volume segue a tendência observada em 2024, quando as importações atingiram o recorde histórico de 28,6 mil milhões de meticais, um crescimento de 38,8% em relação ao ano anterior.
Com 30,9 mil milhões de meticais em bens de consumo importados no trimestre, o arroz ficou atrás apenas dos automóveis (5,9 mil milhões) e do óleo alimentar (5,6 mil milhões). Esta dependência do exterior contrasta com a acentuada quebra da produção interna. Dados do Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE) revelam que, em 2023, o país produziu apenas 161 829 toneladas de arroz, uma queda de 34% face às 245 792 toneladas de 2022, atingindo o nível mais baixo dos últimos cinco anos.
A província da Zambézia liderou a produção nacional, com 48 537 toneladas, seguida de Gaza, com 40 946. A queda acentuada na produção realça a vulnerabilidade da segurança alimentar nacional e a urgência de investimentos estruturais no sector agrícola.
a5639.en:
Mozambique imported rice equivalent to 4.1 billion meticais in the first quarter of this year alone, according to data from the Bank of Mozambique (BdM). This figure represents almost 15% of the total consumer goods purchased abroad in the same period, keeping rice among the three most imported products in the country. The volume follows the trend observed in 2024, when imports reached a historic record of 28.6 billion meticais, a growth of 38.8% compared with the previous year.

With 30.9 billion meticais in consumer goods imported in the quarter, rice was behind only automobiles (5.9 billion) and cooking oil (5.6 billion). This dependence on foreign supply contrasts with the sharp drop in domestic production. Data from the National Institute of Statistics (INE) reveal that in 2023 the country produced only 161,829 tonnes of rice, a fall of 34% from the 245,792 tonnes of 2022, reaching the lowest level of the last five years.

The province of Zambezia led national production, with 48,537 tonnes, followed by Gaza with 40,946. The sharp fall in production highlights the vulnerability of national food security and the urgency of structural investment in the agricultural sector.

ሕወሓት ከሰሞኑ ባወጣው መግለጫ በሰሜን ኢትዮጵያ በነበረው ጦርነት ከቀዬአቸው የተፈናቀሉ ዜጎች ወደ ነበሩበት መመለስ የሚችሉት፣ የትግራይ ክልል ግዛት ወደ ነበረበት ሲመለስ ብቻ ነው ሲል አስታወቀ፡፡
በፕሪቶሪያ ስምምነት መሠረት ጦርነቱ የተገታበትን ሁለተኛ ዓመት አስመልክቶ የአሜሪካ የውጭ ጉዳይ ሚኒስትር አንቶኒ ብሊንከን በሰጡት መግለጫ ላይ ተመሥርቶ ሕወሓት ምላሽ ሰጥቷል፡፡
የአሜሪካ የውጭ ጉዳይ ሚኒስትር ከቀናት በፊት ከጠቅላይ ሚኒስትር ዓብይ አህመድ (ዶ/ር) ጋር በስልክ ባደረጉት ንግግር የፕሪቶሪያ ስምምነት ሁለተኛ ዓመትን አስመልክቶ ውይይት ማድረጋቸውን፣ አሜሪካ ይህ ስምምነት በተሳካ ሁኔታ እንዲፈጸም ለኢትዮጵያ መንግሥት ድጋፏን እንደምታደርግ መገለጹ ይታወሳል፡፡
በመግለጫው በትግራይ ክልል ጠቃሚ ለውጦች መምጣታቸውንና የተኩስ ድምፅ አለመሰማቱን፣ ተፈናቃዮች ወደ ቀዬአቸው መመለሳቸውንና መሠረታዊ አቅርቦቶች መቅረብ መጀመራቸውን የውጭ ጉዳይ ሚኒስትሩ ገልጸዋል፡፡ የሽግግር ፍትሕ ፖሊሲ ሒደት ፍኖተ ካርታ መጠናቀቅን በበጎ እንደሚቀበሉ በመግለጫው ማስታወቃቸው ተገልጿል፡፡
የኢትዮጵያ መንግሥት ተጎጂዎችን ያማከለ የሽግግር ፍትሕ እንዲተገብርና ተዓማኒነት ያለው የአገራዊ ምክክር እንዲከናወን የጠየቁት ብሊንከን፣ በኢትዮጵያ የሚታዩ ሌሎች ግጭቶችን ለመፍታት የፖለቲካ ውይይት እንዲደረግና በአማራ ክልል እየጨመረ የመጣ ያሉት ግጭት እንደሚያሳስባቸው ከጠቅላይ ሚኒስትሩ ጋር መነጋገራቸው ተጠቁሟል፡፡
ይህንን የአሜሪካ መንግሥት መግለጫ ተከትሎ ሕወሓት ባወጣው መግለጫ፣ የትግራይ ተፈናቃዮችን መመለስ የሚቻለው በሕገ መንግሥቱ በተቀመጠው መሠረት የክልሉ የግዛት አንድነትና ሲያስተዳድራቸው የነበሩ አካባቢዎችን መልሶ መቆጣጠር ሲቻል እንደሆነ አስታውቋል፡፡ ይህ ደግሞ በትግራይ ክልል ከአገር መከላከያ ሠራዊት ውጭ ያሉ ኃይሎች መውጣት እንዳለባቸው፣ መተማመን ለመገንባትና ክልሉን ለማረጋጋት፣ እንዲሁም የተፈናቀሉ ዜጎች በክብርና በደኅንነት ወደ ቤታቸው እንዲመለሱ ያደርጋል ብሏል፡፡
የአሜሪካ የውጭ ጉዳይ ሚኒስትሩ በክልሉ የተገኙ ለውጦችንና ችግሮችን ቢገልጹም፣ የተፈናቀሉ ዜጎች ወደ ቤታቸው ተመልሰዋል የሚለውና መሠረታዊ አቅርቦቶች ተስተካክለዋል የሚለው ጉዳይ መሬት ላይ ያለውን እውነታ አያመለክትም ሲል ሕወሓት በመግለጫው ጠቅሷል፡፡ ለዚህ ምንም ዓይነት ተፈናቃዮች ወደ ምዕራብ ትግራይ አለመመለሳቸውን፣ አብዛኞቹ ተፈናቃዮች ከዚህ አካባቢ የመጡ እንደሆኑም በመግለጫው አትቷል፡፡

TPLF says the displaced will return only when Tigray's territory is restored – Reporter – Ethiopian Reporter – #1 Reliable News Source In Ethiopia

In a statement issued in recent days, the TPLF announced that citizens displaced from their homes in the war in northern Ethiopia can return to where they were only when the territory of the Tigray region is restored to what it was.

The TPLF responded on the basis of the statement given by the US Secretary of State, Antony Blinken, marking the second anniversary of the halting of the war under the Pretoria agreement.

It is recalled that the US Secretary of State, in a telephone conversation held a few days earlier with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD), discussed the second anniversary of the Pretoria agreement, and that it was stated that America would provide its support to the Ethiopian government so that the agreement is successfully implemented.

In the statement, the Secretary of State said that important changes have come to the Tigray region, that the sound of gunfire is not heard, that displaced people have returned to their homes, and that basic supplies have begun to be provided. He also announced in the statement that he welcomes the completion of the roadmap of the transitional justice policy process.

Blinken, who asked that the Ethiopian government implement victim-centred transitional justice and that a credible national dialogue be carried out, also indicated that he discussed with the Prime Minister the need for political dialogue to resolve other conflicts seen in Ethiopia, and that he is concerned about what he called the growing conflict in the Amhara region.

Following this statement by the US government, the TPLF, in a statement it issued, announced that the return of Tigray's displaced people is possible only when, in accordance with what is set out in the constitution, the region's territorial integrity and its control over the areas it used to administer are restored. This, it said, requires that forces other than the national defence army withdraw from the Tigray region, and would build trust, stabilise the region, and allow displaced citizens to return to their homes in dignity and safety.

Although the US Secretary of State described the changes and the problems that exist in the region, the claim that displaced citizens have returned to their homes and that basic supplies have been put right does not reflect the reality on the ground, the TPLF noted in its statement. In support of this, the statement also noted that no displaced people at all have returned to Western Tigray, and that most of the displaced come from that area.

It announced that, although the fact that gunfire is no longer heard and that basic supplies have begun may be called positive changes, the presence in the Tigray region of forces other than the national defence army is an obstacle preventing the displaced from returning.

The TPLF, which asked that the international community take part in the transitional justice system, said that a lasting solution must be found by holding meaningful and urgent political dialogue. It also announced that it is ready for the Pretoria agreement to be implemented for the benefit of the community and for dialogue to be held.

Filmmaker Jeffrey Barbee was shocked when he first realised the scale of gas operations in Botswana. A map on the government’s website indicating the distribution of concessions given to multinational energy companies reveals that a good chunk of the Central Kalahari Game Reserve (CKGR) is covered, and it appears that part of the Chobe National Park is too. Among the companies given permission to drill for coal bed methane are SASOL, Anglo American, Exxaro, Kalahari Energy and others.
These concessions fall on environmentally vital lands. The CKGR is the second-largest wildlife reserve in the world, as well as being the ancestral home of the San. The Chobe National Park is home to the world’s largest herd of migrating elephants.
“I was amazed that the whole project had gone ahead in such a widespread way,” Barbee told the Daily Maverick on Wednesday. “Everyone seemed surprised at my interest. When some realised I was a journalist they got very upset very quickly, and by and large no one had any idea what I was talking about regarding the dangers of this process.”
When Barbee spoke to journalists, community members, San activists and lawyers in Botswana, he found that the public was largely unaware that the gas exploration was taking place. “We have heard nothing,” a San rights advocate called Keikabile Mogodu told the Guardian. “We are in the dark.”
This week, the findings contained in Barbee’s film, The High Cost of Cheap Gas, were released, and have met with remarkably little fanfare thus far. Government spokesperson Jeff Ramsay admitted that “Coal bed methane is being prospected in the country”. He also said initially: “Environmental impact assessments and management plans are a legal requirement for all mining in our country.”
But Sasol’s unconventional gas development manager Steve Boden allegedly told the Guardian: “We weren’t required to do an environmental management plan for it but in our opinion it’s best practice that we do.”
The debate over fracking’s environmental damage has been explored repeatedly in these pages, but at the very least, many agree that there is uncertainty over its long-term consequences. Richard Lee, Communications Manager for the Open Society Initiative for Southern Africa (OSISA), which funded Barbee’s film, believes that the government of Botswana’s approach to the issue has been grossly remiss.
“Given the scale of the developments in Botswana and the controversy surrounding the potential effects of unconventional natural gas production in South Africa, Europe and the USA, the government in Gaborone had a clear duty to inform the people – particularly communities that are living in or near the concessions – about gas developments,” Lee told the Daily Maverick. “But they did not do it even though gas operations have been underway for years. The people of Botswana have the right to publicly debate issues of national importance like this and they have not had that opportunity.”
The Botswana government’s comments this week in response to the allegations have been somewhat Mac Maharaj-ish. A statement released by the Ministry of Minerals, Energy and Water Resources initially focused on the distinction between exploration and fracking. “There are currently no fracking operations going on in the country except exploration drilling by various exploration companies,” it said.
That’s not what Barbee has observed.
“I stood at a fracking operation, with pressure truck, chemical mixer, drill and water truck. All the trucks were older ones from the early days of drilling in the US,” he told the Daily Maverick. “It was such an odd feeling to be standing in the middle of the Botswana wilderness looking at an operation just like the ones in my valley in Colorado.”
A further indication that fracking is already taking place appears to be found on the website of Kalahari Energy, discussing its joint venture with Exxaro Coal Botswana. In an article dated 9 July 2010, it states: “This week Exxaro Coal Botswana commenced with the perforation and fracturing of their 5-spot wells which will take them until mid-September to complete. Expertise has been sought from the USA for this programme, which consists of perforating the well’s steel production casing with explosive charges followed by the fracturing of the coals with high pressure water, sand and chemicals.”
A screengrab of another article from Kalahari Energy’s website seen by the Daily Maverick, dated 15 August 2005, explains that water evaporation ponds are under construction. “Initially the ponds will be used to hold the water for hydraulic fracturing of the wells,” it states. Barbee’s film, which will be released next week, apparently contains shots of similar water collection pans now.
But then, late on Wednesday, the Botswana government suddenly seemed to change tack, sending out a different statement. It said it stood by its earlier statement that “there are currently no fracking operations going on in the country except exploration drilling”, repeating those words.
But then it added a little caveat: “No current operations have been given permission to conduct hydraulic fracking…Permission has, however, been given in some instances in the past for the use of industrial explosives in sub-surface fracturing, which some may view as a type of ‘fracking’.” The government also said that this year there has been “a significant decline” on prospecting concessions in the CKGR.
“The government’s claim that gas operations are still at the exploration stage is a smokescreen to cover up the fact that the story has come out,” Lee said. “One geologist told us that they had been flaring gas for two years in one location. Surely the government has a duty to inform people about that, even if it is only exploration?”
The government’s riposte is that all “processes and procedures involving mineral licensing” sit as public documents on its own website.
To date the government of Botswana has had a widely-praised track record on environmental issues and on the handling of its mineral resources. Botswana President Ian Khama was named a 2013 Global Visionary in October. At the time, the organisers put out a press release paying tribute to his government for “piloting pan-African efforts to monitor and safeguard water, minerals, and wildlife – all of which are crucial to future conservation efforts”. A year previously, Khama won a lifetime honorary membership of the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN) for his “life-long commitment to the environment”.
“This expose puts [the government’s] reputation at risk, since the authorities have been handing out concessions inside, and in the buffer zones alongside, globally renowned and biodiversity-rich parks,” Lee said. “The government needs to rapidly explain this contradiction to its own people and the international community.” DM
Read more:
- Botswana faces questions over licenses for fracking companies in Kalahari, in the Guardian
Picture: Jeffrey Barbee

Nampula (Mozambique), 23 Oct (AIM) – Over 5,000 Mozambican small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have already benefited from financial support and technical training, under the “Conecta Negócios Project.”
This project, which is coordinated by the Mozambican Ministry of Finance, is budgeted at 15 million US dollars disbursed by the World Bank.
The initiative is aimed at training, funding and preparing SMEs in order to integrate them into the supply chains of large enterprises in Mozambique, with a focus on the Nacala Logistics Corridor, in the northern province of Nampula.
According to the project expert Joel Sauane, who was speaking to AIM on Wednesday during a supervision mission in Nampula, the project has already reached important milestones in its implementation.
“The training process is progressing in Nampula, Tete and Cabo Delgado provinces, which are the priorities, with the support of the Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) as the project’s co-implementing entity”, he said.
Sauane explained that the training is aimed at instructing the SMEs on how to establish connections with the megaproject operators and the customers in general.
“In the first phase, SMEs receive training in business management, gender inclusion, green competitiveness, and digital skills. In the second phase, they move on to the ISO 9001 certification process, required to supply goods and services to megaprojects, and can then apply for grants”, he said.
Sauane revealed that the overall goal is to train 9,000 SMEs, of which 6,000 have already been trained. The project intends to cover 3,000 SMEs in Nampula, and so far 2,900 have been covered.
“In order to support these companies financally, 15 million dollars in grants are available, divided equally into 7.5 million for microenterprises and 7.5 million for SMEs”, he added.
Business owners from Nampula province who participate in the training programme are already feeling the benefits and report improved performance.
Hegínio Mussequece, from the construction sector, said “we learned tools focused on results. Our hope is to obtain certification that will allow us to participate in major projects underway in Nampula province and beyond. We intend to apply for the grant to leverage our business with the acquisition of equipment.”
Linda Nhalate, from the seafood industry, praised the management skills learned in the training, claiming that they “will help us implement more professional administrative procedures.”
“This will help the company grow. We hope to continue expanding and recruiting more young people as now we are hiring 12 permanent employees and 40 seasonal employees”, she added.
Scheduled for implementation until 2027, Conecta Negócios is a structuring project that aims to prepare Mozambican MSMEs to compete in more demanding markets, positioning them as strategic partners in national economic development.
(AIM)
